classification.difficultyReason: Calculate tax at bracket boundaries, transfer the completed table to supplied axes and describe the horizontal then increasingly steep straight segments, connecting their gradients to tax rates.

inlines.text: Use the tax table to complete this table.
The first two incomes are in the tax-free bracket.

children.prompt: Plot the points on the axis and describe the shape of the curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, tall graph on the right beneath the completion table
spec.description: Blank portrait coordinate grid with taxable income from $0 to $200 000 and tax payable from $0 to $70 000. Horizontal minor intervals are $10 000 and vertical minor intervals are $2 000.
spec.mathematics: Coordinates use x = taxable income / 10000 and y = tax payable / 2000. Plot area is 0 ≤ x ≤ 20 and 0 ≤ y ≤ 35.
spec.answerVisibility: Only axes, ticks, titles and grid are supplied; no plotted points or curve.

answer.short: Plot $(0,0)$, $(18\,200,0)$, $(45\,000,5\,092)$, $(120\,000,29\,467)$ and $(180\,000,51\,667)$. The graph is horizontal at first, then consists of increasingly steep straight segments. The gradient represents the tax rate.
answer.worked: Plot the five completed-table points and join consecutive points with straight segments. The graph is horizontal up to \$18 200, then rises with successive gradients 0.19, 0.325 and 0.37. Each gradient is the marginal tax rate in that bracket, so the graph becomes steeper as taxable income increases.

spec.description: Completed graph showing the five table points joined by straight segments through the tax-bracket boundaries.
spec.mathematics: Points in dollar coordinates are (0,0), (18200,0), (45000,5092), (120000,29467), (180000,51667). The coordinate transformation is x = income / 10000, y = tax / 2000.
